title: Retelling Stories
target_phrases: The message of the story is...

dialogue.title: Book Club Discussion
dialogue.context: Ahmed joins a workplace book club and retells the story they read to a friend who missed the meeting.

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.text: Ahmed, I'm sorry I missed book club yesterday. What book did you discuss?

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: We read 'The Kite Runner' by Khaled Hosseini. It's a powerful story about friendship and redemption.

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.text: I've heard of it! What's it about?

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: The story is about two boys in Afghanistan - Amir and Hassan. Amir comes from a wealthy family, while Hassan is a servant's son.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Yes, but it's complicated. At the beginning, they're very close. They fly kites together and Hassan is incredibly loyal to Amir. Then something terrible happens - Hassan is hurt, and Amir witnesses it but doesn't help.

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.text: Oh no! Why doesn't he help?

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: He's afraid and ashamed. After that, their friendship is destroyed. Amir carries this guilt for years. The story then jumps forward - Amir is an adult living in America when he gets a call that changes everything.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: He learns that Hassan has died, and he has a chance to make things right by helping Hassan's son. In the end, Amir returns to Afghanistan to rescue the boy, facing his past mistakes.

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.text: Wow, that sounds intense. What's the message?

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: I think it's about how it's never too late to do the right thing. The book shows that we can find redemption even after terrible mistakes. It really moved me.

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.text: Thanks for explaining it so well! Now I definitely want to read it.

examples: The story is about a family surviving a natural disaster.
The story is about a woman starting her own business.
The story is about two friends who become enemies.
The story is about a child discovering a secret.
The story is about someone overcoming a difficult challenge.
At the beginning, the character is happy and carefree.
In the middle, everything changes when she loses her job.
At the end, she realizes what's truly important.
At the beginning, they are strangers. By the end, they're best friends.
In the middle of the story, a secret is revealed.
The message is that family is most important.
The theme is about forgiveness and redemption.
The message is that honesty is always best.
The theme is that courage comes in many forms.
The message is about the importance of following your dreams.

listening_exercises.transcript: When retelling a story, focus on the main events, not every detail. Include: who the main characters are, where and when it takes place, the main conflict or problem, key events in order, and how it resolves. Think of it as a movie trailer - give enough information to be interesting but not every scene.
listening_exercises.question: What should you include when retelling a story?
options: Main characters, setting, conflict, key events, resolution

listening_exercises.transcript: Use present tense when summarizing plots, even though the story is in past tense. Say 'The story is about a man who loses his job' not 'was about.' This makes the retelling more immediate and engaging. However, when discussing your experience reading it, use past tense: 'I read it last week' or 'It made me cry.'
listening_exercises.question: What tense should you use when summarizing plots?

listening_exercises.transcript: To avoid spoilers, you can say 'then something unexpected happens' or 'there's a twist at the end' without giving details. This keeps the story interesting for people who haven't read or watched it yet. You can also ask 'Do you want to know what happens, or should I not spoil it?' before revealing major plot points.
listening_exercises.question: How can you avoid spoiling a story?

speaking_tasks.prompt: Retell a story from a book, movie, or TV show you enjoyed. Include the beginning, middle, and end. Don't spoil major twists! Record for 35 seconds.
speaking_tasks.example: I recently watched a movie called 'The Pursuit of Happyness.' The story is about a man named Chris who is struggling financially. At the beginning, he's trying to sell medical equipment while taking care of his young son. Things get worse when his wife leaves and they become homeless. In the middle of the story, Chris gets an opportunity for an unpaid internship at a stock brokerage firm. Despite living in shelters and facing incredible hardships, he works harder than anyone. At the end - and I won't spoil the details - his determination pays off. The message is about never giving up on your dreams, no matter how difficult things get. It's based on a true story, which makes it even more powerful.

speaking_tasks.prompt: Summarize a traditional story or folktale from your culture. What happens and what's the lesson? Record for 30 seconds.
speaking_tasks.example: In Somalia, we have a folktale about a clever rabbit and a proud lion. The story is about a lion who is terrorizing all the animals in the forest. The animals are afraid and don't know what to do. Then a small rabbit volunteers to deal with the lion. At first, the other animals laugh because the rabbit is so small. But the rabbit uses intelligence instead of strength. He tricks the lion into looking at his reflection in a well, making the lion think there's another lion. The lion attacks his own reflection and falls into the well. The message is that intelligence and cleverness are more powerful than strength and size.

writing_tasks.prompt: Write a summary of a book or movie you've experienced. Include: what it's about, main events in order, and the message or theme. (90-110 words)
writing_tasks.example: One of my favorite movies is 'Coco,' an animated film about a Mexican boy named Miguel who dreams of becoming a musician. The story is about Miguel accidentally entering the Land of the Dead on the Day of the Dead holiday. At the beginning, his family forbids music because of a painful history. In the middle, Miguel meets his deceased ancestors and learns the truth about his great-great-grandfather, who abandoned the family to pursue music. There's a beautiful twist about who his real ancestor is. At the end, Miguel returns home with a deeper understanding of family and tradition. The message is that we should honor our ancestors while also pursuing our own dreams. The film beautifully shows how family and personal passion can coexist.

writing_tasks.prompt: Retell a news story or historical event as if it were a story. Include beginning, middle, and end. (70-90 words)
writing_tasks.example: The story of the Apollo 11 moon landing is incredible. At the beginning, America and the Soviet Union were in a space race, competing to be first on the moon. In the middle of the story, NASA prepared three astronauts - Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin, and Michael Collins - for this historic mission. The spacecraft launched in July 1969. There was tremendous tension during the landing - they had only seconds of fuel left. At the end, Armstrong stepped onto the moon and said his famous words: 'One small step for man, one giant leap for mankind.' The message is about human courage and achievement.

grammar_focus.title: Past Tense Narrative
grammar_focus.explanation: Use past tense to tell what happened in a story.
examples: The character went to the city. (simple past)
She was walking when she met him. (past continuous)
He had never seen the ocean before. (past perfect for earlier past)
They lived happily ever after. (simple past)

grammar_focus.title: Reported Speech for Story Dialogue
grammar_focus.explanation: Use reported speech to tell what characters said without direct quotes.
examples: She said she was tired. (reported speech)
He told her to be careful. (reported command)
They said they would help. (reported future)
She asked if he was okay. (reported question)

grammar_focus.title: Sequence Words for Story Order
grammar_focus.explanation: Use sequence words to show order of events in stories.
examples: First, they met. Then, they fell in love. (sequence)
After the war, he returned home. (after + event)
Before she left, she said goodbye. (before + event)
Finally, they lived happily. (conclusion)

cultural_notes: Book clubs are popular in the U.S. - groups of friends meet regularly to discuss books they've read.
Americans often discuss movies, TV shows, and books in casual conversation. Being able to retell stories is a common social skill.
When retelling, it's polite to ask 'Have you seen/read it?' first to avoid spoilers.
Movie review websites like Rotten Tomatoes and book review sites like Goodreads are very popular.
Americans value being able to explain complex stories simply - it shows good communication skills.
'Spoiler alert!' is a common warning before revealing plot details that might ruin the story for others.
